newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 5.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 5.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name products and Consumer Trends. ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

PARIS - A boom in packaging, a recovery in industrial investment and the development of international projects has given a hefty boost to design agencies, with some seeing a return to the strong growth rates of the 1980s. (Strategies)

PARIS - Star French footballers Eric Cantona, David Ginola and Jean-Pierre Papin, all over 30, may have missed out on being shortlisted to play for France in next year's World Cup, but they have each been mopping up advertising contracts for the last few years. (Strategies)

PARIS - Ogilvy & Mather's television spot for the Ford diesel is named as the IPSOS-Strategies advert of the week. The spot, one of few remaining car ads where a woman is used to seduce men, features a petrol pump with a sexy female voice. (Strategies)
LILLE - Euro RSCG is merging its Lille and Brussels branches to win extra market share and attract back budgets from Northern France which have been drawn to Paris. (Les Echos)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

STRASBOURG - European audiovisual watcher l'Observatoire Europeen de l'Audiovisuel says 1996 was the best year for 10 years for cinema attendance in the European Union, with 706 million entries during the year.
PARIS - Polygram may be interested in buying Bouygues's film production unit Ciby 2000. (Les Echos.)

PARIS - Significantly fewer journalists were killed on the job in 1996, but the reporter's trade remains a dangerous one in many parts of the world, press watchdog group Reporters sans Frontieres says. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

PARIS - Remy Cointreau's sales rose 4.8 percent in the year to March 31, 1997, and the company says it took measures during the year to boost its brands, which should help results in 1997/98. (Reuter)

PARIS - French car sales fell 10.3 percent in April, the fourth consecutive monthly drop, as weak demand persisted more than six months after the end of a car-buying incentive programme, the French carmakers association CCFA says. (Reuter)
PARIS - Hippopotamus, the No. 2 theme restaurant chain in France, seeks to push its annual turnover over 500 million francs, notably through franchising. (Le Figaro)
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
For further news and information, see Reuters Advertising & Media Briefing. And visit us on the Internet at http://www.bizinfo.reuters.com
